chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali Majiluwayh - may God be pleased with him - narrated that his father quoted on the authority of Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah al-Barqi, on the authority of al-Sayyari, on the authority of al-Harith ibn al-Dalhath, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abil Hassan Al-Ridha (peace be upon him)

He said: Indeed the Honorable, the Exalted God has ordered three things which are coupled with three other things. He has ordered prayer and alms-tax; whoever prays but does not pay alms-tax, his prayer is not accepted. He has ordered gratitude to God and to parents; whoever does not thank his parents has not thanked God. He has ordered God-consciousness and maintaining kinship ties; whoever does not visit his relatives has not feared God, the Exalted.
ai.seo_question: What are the three pairs of coupled obligations in Islam according to Imam al-Rida?
ai.summary: In this tradition from *Uyun Akhbar al-Rida*, Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) elucidates the inseparable link between ritual worship (ibadat) and social ethics (mu'amalat), a core tenet of Shia jurisprudence. He establishes that prayer is incomplete without zakat, divine gratitude is contingent upon honoring parents, and true God-consciousness (taqwa) is manifested through maintaining kinship ties (silat al-rahim). This triad underscores that spiritual validity in Shia thought is deeply rooted in social responsibility and familial duty.
